client.name: Orrin Home Cover
client.description: A mid-sized UK home insurer piloting an AI support agent that answers policy and claims questions in web chat before handing off to human handlers.

engagement.goal: Define what the support agent must reliably do, what it should do, and what is still unproven, so the team can build an eval suite before widening the pilot.
constraints: FCA Consumer Duty applies: customers must get accurate information and fair outcomes
Claim outcomes must be decided by a licensed human handler
The agent can only read policy documents and claim status; it cannot change records

items.summary: 38% of conversations are claim-status checks. When the customer gives a policy number, the agent returns the correct status in 94% of checks (n=1,212, audited against the claims system).
The agent twice quoted a £250 flood excess from a superseded policy wording; the current excess is £1,000. Root cause: retrieval returned an archived document.

items.source: Complaints data joined to chat logs
items.summary: Conversations handed to a human within 2 minutes of the customer asking had a 1.1% complaint rate; those handed off after 2 minutes had 4.8% (n=640 handoffs).

items.source: Platform team review of the agent's tools
items.summary: get_claim_status requires both policy number and date of birth. Policy documents are retrievable by policy number and effective date; archived wordings are in the same index.
Head of Claims believes the agent could approve small claims under £250 on its own, cutting handling cost.

items.source: Compliance review with the firm's regulatory lead
items.summary: Compliance's reading of the firm's FCA permissions is that a licensed human must decide every claim outcome, regardless of value. The agent may explain process but not approve or decline.

items.source: Offline comparison of two candidate models on 120 historical chats
items.summary: Model B stated a policy term that is not in the wording in 3 of 120 chats; model A did in 9 of 120. Model B's median response time was 1.4s slower.

items.source: Quality review of 30 sampled bereavement and hardship conversations
items.summary: In 4 of 30, reviewers flagged the agent's tone as abrupt for a customer in distress; in all 4 the agent did not offer a human handoff.
6 of 8 asked whether they were talking to a person; 5 said they would trust answers more if told up front it was an AI with a human available.
Respondents who rated the chat said they prefer it to phoning; response rate was under 2% and skewed to resolved conversations.
A team lead has seen customers try to talk the agent into promising discounts or cover changes.
